QUOTE: `#ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member #endif` ... "by default the field is really named `private_foo`" ... "Library code is not the audience. It opts out." ... "`library/common.h:132` ... Every library translation unit gets plain field names."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer shows both branches and states that code defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS (library, some programs) gets plain names, while ordinary application consumers get the `private_`-renamed fields and compile errors.
